summary: Reduced the funnel from 6 steps to 3 (removing intro, details, and verify) and updated the CTA to go directly to email capture with action-oriented copy ("무료로 시작하기" / "Start free") — because every eliminated step removes a ~25–30% drop-off point, and sending users straight to email collection instead of two pre-qualification pages is the single highest-leverage friction reduction in the funnel.

Added social proof (12,000+ users) and a three-item benefit checklist to the landing page, because concrete trust signals and explicit benefit statements remove hesitation and are consistently the highest-leverage conversion lever when a page has minimal content.

Removed the `confirm` step from the funnel, cutting it from 3 steps to 2, because eliminating the post-email confirmation screen removes a high-drop-off friction point where users who already entered their email abandon before completing signup.

Added a user count social proof ("이미 12,000명 이상이 사용 중"), three concrete benefit bullets, and a styled CTA button — social proof with specific numbers and clear benefit scans are the highest-impact conversion elements for users deciding whether to commit.

Added three concrete benefit bullets and a social proof count ("12,000명이 함께하고 있습니다") to the landing page, because removing uncertainty about what you get and showing that others have already signed up are the two highest-leverage conversion factors on a sparse page.

Added three concrete reassurance bullets (no install, data safety, cancel anytime) to the landing page, because users hesitate to sign up when they don't know what they're committing to — addressing these common objections directly on the page removes friction before the click.
